column1: # PIN ASSIGNMENT for the WeAct MiniSTM32H743 (STM32H743VIT6, LQFP100). Each AF number, ADC channel and timer channel is checked against ST DS12110 (Table 9 pin/AF list and Table 10 port alternate-function matrix, LQFP100 columns) and stm32h7xx_hal_gpio_ex.h, except rows marked AF NOT YET VERIFIED. I2C4 is available on PB8/PB9 (AF6) but not together with I2C1 on that pair, which is the design chosen (two buses: I2C1 on PB8/PB9, I2C2 on PB10/PB11). The design avoids every pin the onboard TFT, microSD and QSPI/SPI flash occupy, and uses the DVP pins freely since no camera is fitted. The board's actual header map is in h743-header-pinout.csv. 5V TOLERANCE STILL TO BE CHECKED in DS12110 (the pin must be FT) for PB4, PB5, PA8, PD7, PD10, PD14, PD15 (relay inputs), PA0 (water indicator cathode) and PE4 to PE8 (key lines, pulled toward the 5V rail through the indicator LEDs); the verified statuses below do not cover it. The only port pins NOT on a header are PC13 (user button) and PE3 (user LED); PA13/PA14 are SWD on their own header. Peripheral use: 2 USART RX (the two energy meters), 2 I2C buses, 5 ADC channels (3 NTC and 2 PT1000), TIM1 for the flow meter and the shared zero-cross, and timer-backed outputs for the pump gates. See README.md.

TWO SEPARATE BUSES rather than a mux: 4 pins against the mux's 3, but it deletes the module, 539mm2, AUD 2.18, a failure point and the per-read channel-select at the 100Hz control rate - and it works with both sensors left at 0x7F, so it removes the dependency on the supplier reprogramming addresses. ASSIGNMENT: CONFIRMED DS12110 Table 10 Port B - PB8=I2C1_SCL/PB9=I2C1_SDA (AF4), PB10=I2C2_SCL/PB11=I2C2_SDA (AF4). CORRECTION from the earlier first-pass note: I2C4 was not actually the dead end claimed - I2C4_SCL/SDA IS available on PB8/PB9 too, but as AF6 rather than AF4 (I2C4 shares AF6 on those specific pins because AF4 there is already I2C1's). The real constraint is narrower than 'I2C4 is unusable on this board': no single pin pair serves both I2C1 and I2C4 simultaneously - PB8/PB9 can carry either but not both, and I2C4's other options (PD12/PD13, PF14/PF15) collide with the soldered QSPI flash or aren't bonded on LQFP100 at all. Moot for this design either way: two I2C1/I2C2 buses were chosen over a mux, so I2C4 is not needed

column1: Operator key lines (bidirectional: sink indicator current, read as input with a pull-up)
column6: One line per key group (PWR, MAN, ONE, TWO, PRG). Each carries the group's switch pair (a 1k in series with each switch to ground on the panel) and its indicator cathodes, so an indicator is lit by sinking the line and a key is read as the line pulled low. The OEM draws no external pull-up and relies on the MCU's own, with a 47R in series at the pin; use the H743's internal pull-up and a 47R. Indicator sink current is about 8 mA per element (estimated from 5V, about 2V forward, 300R plus 47R), up to about 16 mA on a two-element line, which is at or above what an H743 pin should sink continuously: check against the pin's rated sink current or sink through spare ULN2003A channels

Replaces the earlier rows of 8 pushbuttons and ~10 LEDs, which counted the indicators twice; the indicators share these lines. 5V tolerance of PE4 to PE8 still has to be checked in DS12110: with the anode rail on, each line is pulled toward the 5V rail through the indicator LEDs when it is not sinking

column8: CONFIRMED DS12110 Table 10: the datasheet's QUADSPI_BK1 mappings match the schematic's QSPI nets, all AF9 except PB6 (BK1_NCS) which is AF10 - the odd one out, worth knowing if these are ever reclaimed as GPIO/AF. These six pins carry the soldered 8MB flash and are the reason I2C4 collides with this board's fixed wiring - CORRECTED framing from the earlier note: I2C4 is not simply unusable, it shares PB8/PB9 (AF6) with I2C1 (AF4) - so it is usable only if I2C1 gives up that pair, and its other option PD12/PD13 sits on these flash pins; PF14/PF15 aren't bonded on LQFP100 at all. Avoid all six flash pins unless the flash is deliberately given up. RECOVERABLE IF NEEDED: the project does not use external flash (the H743 has 2MB internal). Drive PB6 as a GPIO held HIGH so the flash stays deselected - its IO pins are then high-impedance and PB2, PD11, PD12, PD13 and PE2 become usable, recovering 5 of the 6. That also makes I2C4 available again on PD12/PD13. Not done by default: it trades a documented-clean allocation for a shared bus with a soldered device on it
